title: Optimization by Simulated Annealing: An Experimental Evaluation; Part II, Graph Coloring and Number Partitioning
key_finding: Adapts simulated annealing to graph colouring (and number partitioning); the annealing colouring schemes can dominate traditional techniques on certain graph types, at least when large amounts of computing time are available.
limitations: Dated original (1991); results tied to 1991-era hardware/time budgets; abstract notes advantage depends on graph type and long run times.
algorithm: Simulated annealing (several graph-colouring annealing schemes)
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex. Second author shown only as 'C. Aragon' in OpenAlex; middle initial not confirmed. Pre-window foundational item.

title: Exploring the k-colorable landscape with iterated greedy
venue: Cliques, Coloring, and Satisfiability: Second DIMACS Implementation Challenge (DIMACS Series in Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science, AMS)
key_finding: Shows that re-running greedy colouring on a new vertex permutation that respects the colour classes of the previous colouring never increases (and may decrease) the number of colours; the resulting Iterated Greedy (IG) algorithm can optimally colour k-colourable graphs with k up to 60 and n = 1000.
limitations: Dated original (1996); abstract retrieved from OpenAlex was truncated at the end.
algorithm: Iterated Greedy (IG) colouring with permutation-generation heuristics; hybridised with modified tabu search
notes: Draft had '(check DOI)': DOI 10.1090/dimacs/026/13 found via Crossref and confirmed in OpenAlex (type book-chapter, AMS). Pages 245-284 and volume 26 confirmed. Volume title per Crossref container: 'Cliques, Coloring, and Satisfiability'.

title: Graph coloring with physics-inspired graph neural networks
key_finding: Frames graph colouring as multiclass node classification and trains a GNN unsupervised using a Potts-model loss; reports performance on par with or better than existing solvers and scaling to millions of variables, with an end-to-end real-world scheduling use case.
limitations: Unsupervised GNN output may need post-processing for feasibility; comparison set limited to solvers chosen by authors (from abstract only).
algorithm: Physics-inspired GNN (Potts-model loss) for vertex colouring
notes: Metadata match draft. Issue 4 added. OpenAlex biblio returned no page/article number; draft's '043131' is the DOI suffix (APS article-number convention) but was not independently returned, so pages left null.

title: Graph Colouring Meets Deep Learning: Effective Graph Neural Network Models for Combinatorial Problems
venue: 2019 IEEE 31st International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI)
key_finding: A simple GNN trained on random instances to decide colourability generalises to distributions not seen in training and performs better than NeuroSAT, Tabucol and greedy baselines for some distributions; vertex embeddings can be clustered to yield constructive colourings.
limitations: Trained as a binary (decision) classifier; outperforms baselines only for some distributions; small/random instances.
algorithm: Graph neural network (GNN) decision model for k-colourability
notes: Draft fields match. Pages 879-885 added from OpenAlex. OA version is arXiv 1903.04598.

title: A new DSATUR-based algorithm for exact vertex coloring
key_finding: Presents PASS, an exact DSATUR-based branch-and-bound colouring algorithm that applies Sewell's tie-breaking strategy only to a restricted set of vertices; selective application improves overall performance in experiments on 1500 random graphs and a subset of DIMACS benchmarks.
limitations: Exact method; scalability limited to small/medium hard instances (not stated quantitatively in abstract).
algorithm: PASS: exact DSATUR-based branch-and-bound with selective Sewell tie-breaking
notes: OpenAlex publication_year = 2011 (online 18 Oct 2011 per ScienceDirect); issue 39(7) is 2012. Draft year 2012 is the issue year. Abstract from ScienceDirect (OpenAlex abstract null).

title: A Hybrid Approach for Exact Coloring of Massive Graphs
venue: Integration of Constraint Programming, Artificial Intelligence, and Operations Research (CPAIOR 2019), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
key_finding: Combines local search, to find good colourings of massive graphs, with the identification of small subgraphs of potentially large chromatic number that yield strong lower bounds, making it possible to solve extremely large graphs optimally even when they have large k-cores.
limitations: Targets massive sparse real-world networks; exactness depends on finding matching bounds.
algorithm: Hybrid local search + lower-bounding subgraph extraction for exact colouring
notes: All draft fields match (OpenAlex + Springer). OpenAlex spells first author 'Hèbrard'; Springer uses 'Hebrard'. OpenAlex marks closed, but author copies exist on HAL (laas.hal.science/hal-02076298) - not used. Abstract from Springer page.

title: Estimation of Sparse Jacobian Matrices and Graph Coloring Problems
key_finding: Shows that minimising function evaluations for estimating a sparse Jacobian by differences can be treated as a graph colouring problem, leading to efficient algorithms; two of the algorithms are proved optimal for band graphs and numerical evidence indicates near-optimality on practical problems.
limitations: Dated original; application domain is numerical differentiation rather than timetabling.
algorithm: Graph-colouring-based ordering heuristics (incl. smallest-last style orderings) for Jacobian estimation
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex. OpenAlex renders second author 'Morè' (accent error); correct spelling Moré.

title: Improving probability learning based local search for graph coloring
key_finding: Proposes an algorithm that iterates three phases: generate a colouring from a probability matrix, improve it with tabu search, and update the matrix by learning; a group-matching procedure handles colour-class symmetry. Reported as competitive with state-of-the-art algorithms on DIMACS benchmarks.
limitations: Abstract text retrieved via a summarising fetch of ScienceDirect, not verbatim; OpenAlex abstract null.
algorithm: Probability-learning local search with tabu search improvement and group matching
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex. Closed access.

title: A Parallel Graph Coloring Heuristic
key_finding: Presents an asynchronous graph colouring heuristic for distributed-memory parallel computers; on finite-element graphs it scales and usually comes within three or four colours of the best linear-time sequential heuristics, with expected running time O(log n / log log n) for bounded-degree graphs under the P-RAM model.
limitations: Dated original; parallel setting not central to exam timetabling.
algorithm: Jones-Plassmann parallel (random-priority independent set) colouring
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex.

title: Parallel graph coloring algorithms for distributed GPU environments
key_finding: Presents hybrid MPI+GPU colouring approaches (building on Gebremedhin et al. and Deveci et al., implemented with KokkosKernels), extends them to distance-2 and partial distance-2 colouring, and proposes a heuristic to reduce recolouring communication; scales to graphs with 76.7 billion edges on 128 GPUs.
limitations: HPC focus; abstract taken from arXiv preprint version (2107.00075), not the journal page.
algorithm: Distributed MPI+GPU speculative colouring with recolouring (distance-1, distance-2)
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex (article number 102896). OpenAlex abstract null; abstract from arXiv 2107.00075.

title: Set Partitioning via Inclusion-Exclusion
key_finding: Uses inclusion-exclusion and the zeta transform to partition an n-set into k family members in 2^n n^O(1) time, giving exact algorithms of that complexity for chromatic number, chromatic polynomial and related partition problems; with polynomial space, chromatic number is solved in O(2.8718^n).
limitations: Exponential-time exact method; practical only for small graphs.
algorithm: Inclusion-exclusion / zeta-transform exact chromatic number algorithm
notes: All draft fields match OpenAlex.

title: Ising formulations of many NP problems
key_finding: Provides Ising formulations for many NP-complete and NP-hard problems, including all of Karp's 21 NP-complete problems (graph colouring among them), with at most cubically many spins in problem size; intended to aid adiabatic quantum optimisation algorithm design.
limitations: Formulations only; no empirical evaluation.
algorithm: Ising/QUBO formulations (incl. graph colouring)
notes: Title, year, author, volume, DOI match. Article number (draft '5') not returned by OpenAlex/Crossref biblio (only inferable from DOI suffix), so pages null. Frontiers web listing labels it a 'Review' article.

title: Generating a Graph Colouring Heuristic with Deep Q-Learning and Graph Neural Networks
venue: Learning and Intelligent Optimization (LION 17, 2023), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
key_finding: Investigates whether deep reinforcement learning can discover a competitive construction heuristic for graph colouring; ReLCol uses deep Q-learning with a GNN feature extractor and a novel graph parameterisation, and is evaluated against existing construction algorithms on standard benchmarks, showing RL is a promising direction.
limitations: Construction heuristic only (no local search); abstract reports both benefits and limitations relative to classical constructive heuristics such as DSATUR.
algorithm: ReLCol: deep Q-learning + GNN learned vertex-ordering construction heuristic
notes: Matches draft hint 'Watkins, Montana & Branke 2023'. LNCS volume 14286 from WRAP record; pages from OpenAlex/Springer.

title: Graph Coloring problem solving using monte carlo tree search and deep reinforcement learning
key_finding: Proposes a self-learning method combining Monte Carlo tree search with deep reinforcement learning, avoiding manual features and labelled data; reports advantages over existing colouring algorithms and good performance on graphs larger than those seen in training.
limitations: Abstract gives no benchmark names or quantitative margins; closed access.
algorithm: MCTS + deep RL (AlphaZero-style) for graph colouring
notes: Article number 20 from Springer page; OpenAlex gives volume/issue only and displays first author as 'Yang Wenzhu' (name order flipped).

title: Reinforcement learning based local search for grouping problems: A case study on graph coloring
key_finding: Proposes reinforcement learning based local search (RLS) for grouping problems, in which RL extracts information from discovered local optima to guide the search toward promising regions; verified on graph colouring.
limitations: Online publication date (OpenAlex 2016-08-05; ScienceDirect 4 Aug 2016) falls before the window start.
algorithm: Reinforcement learning based local search (RLS)
notes: Discovered. Outside window by ~2 months (online Aug 2016); the volume 64 issue date was not retrieved. Include only as a dated precursor.

title: Mapping graph coloring to quantum annealing
key_finding: Maps a pseudo-Boolean graph-colouring formulation (via SATyrus) to a QUBO and solves it with classical SA, a simulated quantum environment and a D-Wave quantum annealer; both SA and QA produce good heuristics for this problem, although more solutions were found with QA.
limitations: Small instances constrained by D-Wave hardware; results depend on penalty weights.
algorithm: QUBO formulation + quantum annealing (D-Wave) vs simulated annealing
notes: Discovered. Metadata from Crossref (OpenAlex record rate-limited); online 16 Nov 2020, issue Dec 2020. Abstract and conclusion read from the Springer PDF.

title: Two Stage Quantum Optimization for the School Timetabling Problem
key_finding: Notes that timetabling with only hard constraints reduces to graph vertex colouring, and proposes the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) as a heuristic for school timetabling, simulated on small examples with 42 qubits, demonstrating feasibility of hybrid quantum-classical approaches.
limitations: Gate-based QAOA in simulation, not quantum annealing; toy-sized instances only. Abstract text came through a summarising fetch.
algorithm: QAOA (QUBO/Ising-based) two-stage timetabling via graph colouring
notes: Discovered. Second author family name given as 'de Santiago' in OpenAlex; confirm preferred citation form. Closed access.

title: A Performance Comparison of Graph Coloring Algorithms
venue: International Journal of Intelligent Systems and Applications in Engineering
key_finding: Compares First Fit, Largest Degree Ordering, Welsh-Powell, Incidence Degree Ordering, DSATUR and RLF on DIMACS benchmark graphs; RLF and DSATUR are found sufficient while First Fit is generally deficient, with Welsh-Powell fastest to reach optimal results on some sets and RLF best on the rest.
limitations: Small-venue journal; DIMACS graphs only; no timetabling instances.
algorithm: Comparative study of greedy constructive heuristics (FF, LDO, WP, IDO, DSATUR, RLF)
notes: Discovered. OpenAlex lists only 'Murat Aslan'; publisher page lists Aslan & Baykan. OpenAlex date 2016-12-15; publisher 'issued' 30 Dec 2016 - both inside window.

title: A robust and efficient algorithm for graph coloring problem based on Malatya centrality and sequent independent sets
key_finding: Proposes the Malatya Sequent Independent Set Coloring Algorithm, which builds successive independent sets by repeatedly selecting the vertex with lowest Malatya centrality; tested on social-network, random and benchmark graphs and reported to give polynomial-time solutions with high performance. The publisher page lists Welsh-Powell, greedy, DSATUR and RLF as comparison baselines.
limitations: Single-author; baseline list taken from a summarising fetch of the article page, not verified in full text.
algorithm: MSISCA (centrality-guided independent-set colouring) vs Welsh-Powell/greedy/DSATUR/RLF
notes: Discovered. Gold OA.

title: Matheuristic Variants of DSATUR for the Vertex Coloring Problem
venue: Metaheuristics (MIC 2024), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
key_finding: Extends DSATUR with matheuristic operators: clique/partial-optimal-colouring initialisation, an ILP formulation for local optimisation during construction, and dual bounds from local optimisation; the computational analysis exposes inefficiencies of DSATUR and its comparative strengths and weaknesses.
limitations: Abstract text came through a summarising fetch of the Springer page (OpenAlex abstract null).
algorithm: DSATUR + ILP-based matheuristic variants
notes: Discovered. LNCS volume 14754 from Springer page.

title: The performance analysis of hyper-heuristics algorithms over examination timetabling problems
venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI)
key_finding: Compares hill climbing, simulated annealing, great deluge and tabu search as hyper-heuristic move acceptance on the Carter (Toronto) uncapacitated exam benchmarks (200,000 iterations each) and examines a Kempe chain low-level heuristic; tabu search gave the best solution in 13 instances and the Kempe chain LLH tended toward better solutions.
limitations: Mid-tier venue; random LLH selection; fixed iteration budget rather than time.
algorithm: Selection hyper-heuristic with Kempe-chain low-level heuristic (HC/SA/GD/TS acceptance)
notes: Discovered. Directly uses Toronto instances. Verified via OpenAlex and journal page.

title: Multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing for the ITC-2007 capacitated examination timetabling problem
key_finding: Multi-neighbourhood SA for ITC-2007 capacitated exam timetabling combining existing and new neighbourhoods that exploit the disconnected structure of the conflict graph and handle room assignment; with principled tuning and ablation it competes with state-of-the-art solvers and finds several new best solutions.
limitations: Kempe evidence is from the PATAT 2022 proceedings version, which defines a KempeChain(e,p,r) move that reassigns conflicting exams until no new conflicts remain; the journal abstract does not name Kempe chains and this was not checked in the journal full text.
algorithm: Multi-neighbourhood simulated annealing incl. Kempe-chain move
notes: Discovered. OpenAlex publication_date 2023-12-19 (online); volume 28(2) is 2025. Cite as 2025 (online 2023).

title: Efficient Hybridization of Quantum Annealing and Ant Colony Optimization for Coloring DIMACS Graph Instances
key_finding: Hybridises ACO and quantum annealing for graph colouring on 100 DIMACS instances; QA alone gave better chromatic numbers but excessive runtime on large instances, ACO was faster on simple cases but weaker on complex ones, and the hybrid achieved optimal/best-known results on complex graphs with less time on large instances (Friedman and Nemenyi tests).
limitations: Closed access; abstract came through a summarising fetch of the Springer page.
algorithm: Hybrid ant colony optimisation + quantum annealing
notes: Discovered. Also relevant to A32 (quantum annealing). Article number 29 from Springer page; OpenAlex gives volume/issue only.

title: Physarum-Based Ant Colony Optimization for Graph Coloring Problem
venue: Advances in Swarm Intelligence (ICSI 2019), Lecture Notes in Computer Science
key_finding: Uses the positive-feedback mechanism of a Physarum mathematical model to optimise ACO pheromone-matrix updating for graph colouring; reported to outperform standard ACO and other methods in efficiency, stability and computational cost.
limitations: Short conference paper; abstract came through a summarising fetch of the institutional repository; benchmarks not named in abstract.
algorithm: Physarum-inspired ant colony optimisation (PM-ACO) for colouring
notes: Discovered. LNCS 11655 from repository page; pages from OpenAlex.

title: Solving examination timetabling problem in UniSZA using ant colony optimization
key_finding: Applies an ant system (ACO) to the university examination timetabling problem at UniSZA.
limitations: Low-quality venue (IJET, Science Publishing Corporation); 4-page paper; abstract reports no quantitative results. Use only as evidence that ACO is still applied to exam timetabling.
algorithm: Ant System (ACO) for exam timetabling
notes: Discovered. Pages: publisher 132-135, OpenAlex 132-132 (publisher used). Published 6 Apr 2018. Family-name split of 'Mohd Nordin Abdul Rahman' assumed as 'Abdul Rahman' - check.
